turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): alfie? on the chair for me, just a temperature before you go in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): no. get off.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): alfie, two seconds. sorry, he's knackered, we were up from two with his eyes glued shut.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): mm. thirty six point nine. pulse one hundred and eight, he's just cross.
[SEG0005] person_4 (DOCTOR): right. the eyes.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): yeah they're red and sticky, proper gunk in them. school won't take him without a note.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): itchy. hate it.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): one eye or both.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): left one, three days ago. yesterday the right one started. both now.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): pain.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): no!
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no he doesn't say it hurts. just rubs them.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): light bother him.
[SEG0014] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no. telly's been on all morning.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): any temperature at home.
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): not now. he had a cold last week, sniffles and a cough, that's gone, then this.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): eating.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): a bit off his food. um he did ask for crisps in the car though, random.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): any reactions to medicines.
[SEG0020] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): penicillin. he's allergic. came out in hives all over and his lip swelled up, he was two.
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): eczema. asthma.
[SEG0022] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): eczema on his arms, yes. no asthma. we use the greasy cream, diprobase, the big tub, at night. and pink calpol, five mils, when he's grotty.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): want the pink one.
[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): not now love. oh and i put those yellow drops in yesterday, cloramphenicol from boots, but i stopped them this morning, he screamed the place down.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): right, you stopped them. look up.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): don't. get off.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): no ulcer. conjunctivae red both sides, gunk in the corners, corneas clear. viral conjunctivitis after the cold. not bacterial.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): so no antibiotic then. the class whatsapp has been a nightmare about it, anyway.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): no antibiotic. nothing from the penicillin family either. warm water, clean cotton pad, wipe outwards, new pad each eye, his own towel, wash your hands.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): he can go back once the stickiness eases. i'll do the note.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): they were quite sharp on the phone.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): reception will print the note. thursday morning the nurse takes a swab from the eye, half eight. nothing in the eyes that morning, no drops and no ointment.
[SEG0033] person_1 (NURSE): thursday half eight, eye swab, i'll book him on my list.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): and i'll see him in two weeks.
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): what if it's still sticky.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): if the swab is borderline we do bloods. if it does not settle we might send him to ophthalmology.
[SEG0037] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): bloods, he's five, he'll hate it.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): only if the swab is borderline, not booked now. two weeks here either way. if the redness spreads or he won't open an eye, come back the same day.

spec.situation: Parent with a child with red sticky eye after a cold; school wants a note; one eye then both; no eye pain; doctor advises hygiene, no antibiotic, explains return advice.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
